summary: Feed s166_triple to IDS is degraded: 48.6% one-way TCP sessions (needs both directions), microbursts to 1.80 Gbps overload 1 Gbps port, and 66.6% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% tolerance. Duplicates, VLANs and drops are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / SPAN is delivering only one direction for ~half of TCP sessions. Likely SPAN configured to mirror TX or RX only, or TAPs on asymmetric paths not aggregated together, so return traffic never reaches IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, stream tracking and signature matching. With 54/111 sessions one-way, IDS will miss handshakes, fail to detect attacks and generate false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS port so bidirectional sessions are complete for stateful inspection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic microbursts peak at 1.80 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (180% overload, 2 intervals). Packet broker is sending line-rate bursts without load-balancing or shaping.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC will drop packets during bursts, causing missed flows, incomplete sessions and blind spots for detection. Sustained overload degrades IDS performance and APM/NDR accuracy.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple 1 Gbps tool ports or a higher-capacity IDS cluster to keep per-port utilization below 80% and prevent burst drops; slicing not viable as IDS needs full payload.

findings.root_cause: 66.6% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) exceeding IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is increasingly opaque without decryption at the visibility layer.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for inspection but cannot analyze encrypted payloads, reducing detection coverage to metadata only and missing payload-based exploits.

recommended_fix.why: Provide decrypted traffic to IDS via centralized SSL visibility appliance or selective decryption policy; alternatively filter known trusted encrypted flows if decryption not possible.
